proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof (definition of H, measurability, local bound); Simon Ch. 4, 3.14 (chapter-04.txt lines 366–381) requires a μ_V-measurable H, and the bound on compact sets is the hypothesis 3.15 (chapter-04.txt line 385) used afterwards. Notation: E := ℝ^P, e_1, …, e_P the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.single j 1), T^* the adjoint of T ∈ L(E, E) (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint), Dpr(x) := fderiv ℝ pr x ∈ L(E, L(E, E)).
1. The algebraic map. Define F : L(E, L(E, E)) × L(E, E) → E by F(B, q) := Σ_j (B(qe_j))^*(qe_j). F is continuous: (B, q) ↦ qe_j and (B, q) ↦ B(qe_j) are continuous (evaluation of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, Continuous.clm_apply), the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence and hence continuous, evaluation (T, w) ↦ Tw is continuous, and a finite sum of continuous maps is continuous.
2. The set G := N ∩ U. We have N ∩ U = closure(N) ∩ U: the inclusion ⊆ is clear, and if z ∈ closure(N) ∩ U but z ∉ N, then z ∈ (closure(N) ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, which is impossible. Hence G is the intersection of a closed set and an open set, so it is Borel measurable.
3. Definition of H. Let H(x) := F(Dpr(x), p(x)) for x ∈ G and H(x) := 0 otherwise, i.e. H is the indicator of G applied to x ↦ F(Dpr(x), p(x)). For x ∈ N ∩ U this gives H(x) = Σ_j (Dpr(x)[p(x)e_j])^*(p(x)e_j), which is the third claimed property.
4. Measurability. The map x ↦ Dpr(x) is Borel measurable for every function pr (measurable_fderiv), and it takes values in a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable). With the hypothesis on p, x ↦ (Dpr(x), p(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk); composing with the continuous F (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable) and taking the indicator of the measurable set G (AEStronglyMeasurable.indicator) shows that H is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
5. Local bound. Let K ⊆ U be compact. The set K ∩ closure(N) is compact (IsCompact.inter_right) and, since K ⊆ U, it is contained in closure(N) ∩ U = N ∩ U (step 2), hence in N ⊆ O. Since O is open and pr is C¹ on O, Dpr is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), so there is C with ‖Dpr(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ K ∩ closure(N) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Put Λ := P·max(C, 0) ≥ 0. Let x ∈ K. If x ∈ G, then x ∈ K ∩ closure(N), so ‖Dpr(x)‖ ≤ max(C, 0). For each j, u_j := p(x)e_j satisfies ‖u_j‖ ≤ ‖p(x)‖·‖e_j‖ ≤ 1, and ‖(Dpr(x)u_j)^*u_j‖ ≤ ‖(Dpr(x)u_j)^*‖·‖u_j‖ = ‖Dpr(x)u_j‖·‖u_j‖ ≤ ‖Dpr(x)‖·‖u_j‖² ≤ max(C, 0), since the adjoint preserves the operator norm (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map). By the triangle inequality ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j max(C, 0) = Λ. If x ∉ G, then H(x) = 0 and ‖H(x)‖ = 0 ≤ Λ. Thus ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ K (this also covers K ∩ closure(N) = ∅ and P = 0), which is the second claimed property.
key_steps: F(B, q) := Σ_j (B(qe_j))^*(qe_j) is continuous, and N ∩ U = closure(N) ∩ U is Borel.
H := 1_{N∩U}·F(Dpr(·), p(·)) has the required formula on N ∩ U and is a.e. strongly measurable (measurable_fderiv, measurability of p, continuity of F).
On compact K ⊆ U, K ∩ closure(N) is a compact subset of O where Dpr is continuous, so ‖Dpr‖ ≤ C there and ‖H‖ ≤ P·max(C, 0) on K.
